Header: Ralstonia solanacearum ዝዝዝዝዝ ዝዝዝዝዝ ዝዝዝ in Amharic language)

Prevention: Use disease free planting soil or fields that are free from the disease
Use disease free planting rhizomes from the known sources or rhizome/seeding from tissue culture
Use the appropriate or recommended planting space both between plants and planting rows to avoid transmission through contact.
Planting in raised beds or ridges
Rotate ginger with crops that are not hosts of the disease, such as maize, taro, sorghum
Do not intercrop or rotate ginger with solanaceous crops such as potato, tomato, pepper, tobacco, eggplant
Harvest on time to minimize crop exposure to the disease if the field is already infected
Disinfect all farm tools by dipping in a disinfectant (household bleach diluted 1 part with 4 parts water)
Ensure farmers start working from disease-free areas before moving to affected ones to prevent spread
Monitoring: Monitor for water-soaked spots/lesions on both pseudo-stem and leaves after emergence of the ginger plant
Daily monitoring/observation for wilted yellow leaves which progress from the bottom upward, affecting the younger leaves and rapidly turning to yellow-brown
Observe rapid yellowing due to ginger bacterial wilt pathogen within 3-5 days of water-soaked symptom emergence.
Monitor for rotting and a bad smell at the collar region or at the junction of the pseudo-stem and rhizomes
Observe white, milky bacteria streaming by cutting and suspend the pseudo-stem or rhizome in clean beaker filled with clean water.
Immediate harvesting and drying for consumptions if the rhizome sets yields
Direct Control: As soon as symptoms are seen, uproot infected plants and burn them
Restrictions: There are no chemical pesticides currently registered in
Ethiopia for management of this disease
